company: Tuya Smart (Hangzhou) — BLE configuration SDK (com.thingclips.sdk.bluetooth Android SDK)
UUID_purpose: GATT Service observed in Android app com.grameenphone.alo but declared in third-party SDK package `com.thingclips.sdk.bluetooth` as Java field `qpppdqb`. The host APK's vendor is NOT the UUID owner; the SDK author is. Classification source: file-level-default. Phase-4 SDK identification: Tuya BLE config SDK — UUID base `7475-7961-626c-636f6e666967` decodes ASCII to `tu` `ya` `bl` `config`. Field names SERVER / WRITE / NOTIFY (uuids 00001000/1001/1002 in that namespace). The other UUID16s (1910/1912/1920) are obfuscated tokens in the same Tuya SDK, plus 7fdd = Telink mesh-test (Tuya often uses Telink chips). Observed in 6 host apps including IoT Solution AiDot, Grameenphone alo, Coclean Degrii, ElegrP home, Movinghub, Xtreme Cables..

company: Android Studio BLE example template
UUID_purpose: Placeholder UUID from an Android BLE GATT-server tutorial — the field name CHAR_UUID_YOU_CAN_CHANGE literally instructs the developer to replace it. Sibling 12345678-9012-3456-7890-123456789012 is the corresponding SERVICE_UUID_YOU_CAN_CHANGE. Phase-4 SDK identification: Default UUID placeholders from the Android Studio BLE service-creation template — `SERVICE_UUID_YOU_CAN_CHANGE` and `CHAR_UUID_YOU_CAN_CHANGE` field names are verbatim from the template's TODO comments. Observed in 4 unrelated Korean abookn-template apps published by xidsystem (com.bsks/ggu/jau/kbc.*_abookn) that all forked the same starter project. These ARE real BLE UUIDs (the apps actually advertise / scan with them) but they identify the template, not any specific vendor..
